tagline: A brand-new UNESCO World Heritage archipelago where the islands still wait days for a boat.
summary: The Marquesas — Te Henua Enata, 'the Land of Men' — were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in July 2024, putting one of the Pacific's most dramatic archipelagos on the world's travel map. Yet moving between Nuku Hiva, Hiva Oa, Ua Pou and their neighbours still means an expensive small-plane hop or waiting for the Aranui 5, the mixed cargo-cruise freighter that is the islands' lifeline. There is no lagoon here — these are open-ocean channels between towering volcanic islands — which is precisely why a long-range hybrid foiling mesh, not short electric hops, is the honest architecture: smooth, fast inter-island links where today there is essentially no scheduled boat at all.

demand_signals.label: Fresh UNESCO World Heritage status
demand_signals.value: Inscribed 26 July 2024 as 'Te Henua Enata — The Marquesas Islands' (mixed cultural + natural site)
demand_signals.note: A once-in-a-generation demand catalyst for a remote archipelago — visitation and cruise interest are climbing off a tiny base

demand_signals.label: The lifeline is a freighter
demand_signals.value: Aranui 5 — a ~250-passenger mixed cargo-cruise ship — is the main cargo carrier AND principal sea link, on ~12-day round trips from Papeete
demand_signals.note: When the islands' flagship transport is a cargo ship on a multi-week rotation, any scheduled fast inter-island service is a step-change

demand_signals.label: Air access is scarce and expensive
demand_signals.value: Papeete↔Nuku Hiva is a 3.5-hour, ~1,400 km flight; one-way fares routinely ~US$470+
demand_signals.note: Inter-island flights run on small ATR/Twin Otter aircraft with limited seats; weather and load cancellations strand visitors between islands

demand_signals.label: French Polynesia tourism at record levels
demand_signals.note: The territory is actively spreading visitation beyond Bora Bora/Moorea; the Marquesas are the flagship 'next frontier' itinerary, anchored by Nuku Hiva by Pearl Resorts and Hiva Oa's Gauguin/Brel heritage

use_cases.title: The northern-southern group link
use_cases.body: Taiohae (Nuku Hiva) and Atuona (Hiva Oa) are the archipelago's two anchors, ~89 nm apart across open ocean with no scheduled boat. A Quanta-LR running this trunk turns a flight-or-freighter problem into a ~3.5-hour smooth crossing, foiling above the swell that makes conventional launches punishing.

use_cases.title: Short-channel island pairs
use_cases.body: A few legs are genuinely short: Hiva Oa ↔ Tahuata across the Bordelais Channel (~10 nm) and Nuku Hiva ↔ Ua Pou (~25 nm). These village-to-village hops — today served by communal boats and chartered bonitiers — fit all-electric service in fair-weather windows, feeding the long-range mesh.

use_cases.title: Heritage-circuit expedition charter
use_cases.body: UNESCO inscription is built on sites spread across six inhabited islands — Taipivai and Hatiheu valleys, Puamau's tiki, Fatu Hiva's Bay of Virgins. A long-range foiling charter strings them into a single multi-day circuit no aircraft can serve, with zero charging dependency on islands that have none.

use_cases.title: Inter-village coastal service
use_cases.body: On Nuku Hiva itself, road links between Taiohae and the northern valleys (Hatiheu, Anaho) cross brutal mountain switchbacks; a coastal foiling shuttle around the island's bays is faster than the 4x4 and opens valley communities to day visitation.

journeys.today: No scheduled boat. Either an Air Tahiti small-plane hop (limited seats, weather-prone, expensive) or wait for the Aranui 5's cargo rotation — visitors simply don't move between the two anchor islands freely.
journeys.with_navier: A ~89 nm Quanta-LR crossing in roughly 3.5 hours, flying above the inter-island swell — the first real scheduled sea link between the northern and southern groups.

journeys.today: The Bordelais Channel funnels wind and swell; the ~10 nm hop is a wet, lurching ride in open communal boats and fishing skiffs.
journeys.with_navier: A 25-minute foiling hop, dry and stable above the channel chop — turning Tahuata's wood-carving villages into an easy half-day from Hiva Oa.

journeys.today: ~25 nm of exposed water to the archipelago's most photogenic island (the basalt spires of Ua Pou) — served irregularly by small boats and a short bumpy flight.
journeys.with_navier: An under-an-hour foiling crossing in fair-weather windows, with the long-range fleet covering heavy-swell days — a dependable daily link where none exists.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Honest scope: only the short channels fit all-electric service — Hiva Oa↔Tahuata (~10 nm), Nuku Hiva↔Ua Pou (~25 nm), and intra-island coastal runs between valley villages. These are open-ocean legs, not lagoon water, so electric service operates in sea-state windows and feeds the long-range mesh rather than forming the spine.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR is the network spine. The defining legs exceed the 70 nm electric envelope: Taiohae↔Atuona ~89 nm (sealed routing), Hiva Oa↔Fatu Hiva ~40 nm of fully exposed ocean best served long-range, Nuku Hiva↔Ua Huka, and ultimately the ~750 nm Papeete connection — all within hybrid range with zero dependence on island charging infrastructure, which the Marquesas do not have.

competitive_landscape: The sea today belongs to the Aranui 5 — a beloved half-cargo, half-cruise freighter that is the islands' supply lifeline and biggest tourism vehicle on ~12-day Papeete rotations — plus communal municipal boats, fishing bonitiers doing informal passenger runs, and occasional expedition cruise calls. Air Tahiti's small turboprops carry most inter-island passengers at high fares with frequent weather disruption. Nobody offers scheduled fast sea links between the islands: the lifeline operators prove the demand and the dependency; the absence of any passenger-first vessel is the gap.

precedents.what: ~$100M, ~100-vessel electric foiling network with JIH Global, first 5 vessels in 2026
precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that a dispersed-archipelago foiling network can be built and phased at national scale — the Marquesas are the long-range complement to that playbook.

seasonality: No cyclone exposure to speak of — the Marquesas sit close to the equator, outside French Polynesia's main cyclone belt — so the season never closes. The constant is the open-ocean swell and east-southeast trades funnelling between islands: leeward (western) coasts and deep bays like Taiohae stay workable while windward channels get rough. Foiling above the swell is the whole value proposition here; the long-range hybrid platform keeps schedules honest when electric-leg windows close.
regulatory_note: French maritime law applies via the Direction Polynésienne des Affaires Maritimes — the same established certification path as the rest of French Polynesia. The 2024 UNESCO inscription brings a formal management plan for the listed cultural and marine sites: a quiet, zero/low-emission fleet aligns directly with the heritage-protection mandate, and the territory and communes actively seek transport solutions that serve resident connectivity, not just tourism — a public-service framing that strengthens any operating partnership.
